title: ALP Build Plan v1
description: The reference machine-readable build plan `scripts/alp_orchestrate/buildplan.py::emit_build_plan` renders for a resolved board.yaml project. Python Tan normally creates the equivalent plan in process and accepts this form through `--plan-from`; it remains the parity/interoperability contract settled with alp-sdk-vscode and tan-cli. One entry per non-`off` core slice carries its command, config artefact contents, app source dir, shared generated artefacts, and planning warnings. Every artefact carries full `contents` so materialisation stays pure IO. camelCase keys form a CLI-consumer contract, not in-repo YAML. Stability: schemaVersion 1 is locked with tan-cli; bump it and record the change in CHANGELOG before a breaking change.

schemaVersion.description: Build-plan contract version. Independent of board.yaml's own schema_version.

generatedBy.description: Identifies the emitting tool (currently the literal 'scripts/alp_orchestrate.py'). Informational only -- not part of the locked consumer contract.

sdkVersion.description: The `version:` field from metadata/sdk_version.yaml at emit time -- the single source of truth for the SDK release version. Additive, schemaVersion 1 (no bump). Informational provenance, not part of the locked consumer contract.

sdkCommit.description: Short git commit (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) of the alp-sdk checkout that produced this plan. null when git or the .git directory isn't available (e.g. a wheel-installed CLI with no checkout) -- never fails the emit. Additive, schemaVersion 1 (no bump). Informational provenance, not part of the locked consumer contract.

planPathMode.description: Issue #865, additive under schemaVersion 1 (no bump): 'tokened' means every checkout/project-anchored absolute path this plan would otherwise embed is instead a literal `${SDK_ROOT}` / `${PROJECT_ROOT}` / `${PYTHON}` token (see `env.ALP_SDK_ROOT`, `envAppendPath`, `slices[].appDir`, and the `-DPython3_EXECUTABLE=`/`-DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=`/`-DSB_CONF_FILE=`/`west build`-appdir command args) -- tan-cli (PR #24) substitutes them at materialise time, rather than the SDK baking in this run's absolute checkout path. Required by tan-cli's substitution step; a consumer pinned to a pre-#865 plan shape simply won't see this key.

boardYaml.description: POSIX-style path to the board.yaml this plan was resolved from, as passed to emit_build_plan (issue #596: every relative path elsewhere in the plan is anchored on this file's own directory, never the emitting process's CWD).

buildRoot.description: POSIX-style path to the root build directory every slice's buildDir and the shared artefacts are nested under.

executionPolicy.description: SDK-owned skip-vs-fail policy the executor MUST apply when dispatching a slice's `command`, so a plan consumer stops hand-porting that logic. Additive, schemaVersion 1.

unknownBackend.description: Outcome when a slice's `backend` has no known tool mapping. Currently always 'fail'.

missingTool.description: Outcome when `command.tool` cannot be resolved to an executable by the executor. Currently always 'skip' (normal on a dev host missing one toolchain). Deliberately NOT phrased as "isn't found on the executor's PATH" (issue #1314): PATH is the executor's *search* input for a bare identity, but what gets spawned is the resolved path, never the bare name -- see ADR-0020's Security consequence and its Amendment (2026-08-12), plus tan-cli#510 / PR alplabai/tan-cli#530. An absolute `command.tool` that does not exist therefore lands on this outcome with no PATH involved at all.

nullCommand.description: Outcome when a slice's `command` is null (this emitter had no valid command to produce -- see `slices[].command`). Currently always 'skip'.

slices.description: One entry per core whose resolved os is not `off`, sorted by coreId. A core this emitter cannot yet produce a build command for (e.g. missing app/board/image, or an app-only Yocto slice with no recipe:) is still carried here with command: null plus a matching entry in `warnings` -- never silently dropped.

backend.description: The slice's resolved os (Slice.os). `off` cores never reach the plan, so this enum excludes it.

appDir.description: This slice's app source directory, independent of `command` -- lets tooling watch the app source without reverse-engineering it out of a yocto/zephyr/baremetal-shaped command (issue #597). null when the slice has no app source dir to report, e.g. a Yocto slice built from the `alp-image-edge` stock-image token rather than an `app:` path. Issue #865 (`planPathMode: tokened`): a project-anchored app is `${PROJECT_ROOT}/<relpath>` (or exactly `${PROJECT_ROOT}`); an SDK-owned app (the stock M-core shim) is `${SDK_ROOT}/<relpath>`; the rare app resolving under neither root is left as a genuine absolute path and paired with an `appdir-unrooted` warning rather than silently mis-rooted.

configArtefacts.description: This slice's own generated config artefact(s) (alp.conf / local.conf), or an empty array when the slice's os has none -- `baremetal` always has none; its `-D` args are available on request via the standalone `--emit cmake-args` mode instead. Byte-identical to what a consumer's own materialise step writes to buildDir.

path.description: POSIX-style path (under buildDir) the consumer should write `contents` to.

contents.description: Full file contents, ready to byte-write verbatim.

toolchain.description: This slice's compiler identity (#610 §4 per-slice tooling index), grounded in the SoM preset's `topology.<core>.toolchain` default or a project's `cores.<core>.toolchain` override (board.schema.json, issue #964) -- never invented. A field genuinely not derivable for this slice's runtime is null rather than guessed (e.g. a Yocto slice's exact GCC triple depends on the Yocto build's own TUNE_FEATURES/TCLIBC, outside board.yaml/SoM metadata).

targetTriple.description: GCC target triple for this slice's compiler (e.g. `arm-zephyr-eabi` for a Zephyr Cortex-M slice, which is both the Zephyr SDK toolchain directory name and its real GCC triple). null when not derivable (e.g. Yocto -- the triple depends on the Yocto build's own TCLIBC/TUNE_FEATURES).

compiler.description: Compiler executable name for this slice (e.g. `arm-zephyr-eabi-gcc`). null when not derivable.

sysroot.description: Cross-compile sysroot path for this slice, when the runtime has one. Always null today -- Zephyr bundles its own libc per architecture inside the Zephyr SDK (no conventional sysroot), and Yocto's sysroot lives inside the Yocto build tree, not in board.yaml/SoM metadata.

id.description: Stable toolchain identifier, taken verbatim from the SoM preset's `topology.<core>.toolchain` default, or a project's `cores.<core>.toolchain` override when set (e.g. `arm-zephyr-eabi`, `poky-glibc`, `llvm`) -- the same field `system-manifest.yaml`'s `slices[].toolchain` already surfaces. null when neither the SoM preset nor board.yaml declares one for this core.

artifacts.description: Deterministic OUTPUT paths under `buildDir` for this slice (#610 §4) -- the WHERE, not a promise the files exist yet (they don't until the slice is actually built). Zephyr's own CMake layout fixes these paths (cmake/modules/kernel.cmake + the top-level CMakeLists.txt), rooted at west's own build tree `<buildDir>/build/` -- the slice's `command` runs with cwd=`buildDir` and NO `-d`, so west appends its default `build` level itself. A consumer reads these paths VERBATIM and must not re-derive them from `buildDir`: through alp-sdk issue #1360 this block omitted that `build/` level and named files west never wrote. A Yocto slice's real output lands under the Yocto build tree's own deploy dir (outside this slice's buildDir), so it stays all-null. A baremetal slice's executable NAME is the app's own CMakeLists.txt to pick -- never guessed here -- but its `outputDir` is pinned by the `-DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=` arg the slice's own configure carries (alplabai/tan-cli#550). A slice whose `command` is null (blocked -- see the matching `warnings` entry) reports an all-null block: nothing will ever configure its build dir, so any path here would be pinned by a command that never runs.

elf.description: POSIX-style path to the slice's ELF output (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/zephyr/zephyr.elf`). null when this runtime has no single predictable ELF output (yocto, baremetal).

map.description: POSIX-style path to the linker map file (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/zephyr/zephyr.map`). null when not derivable.

bin.description: POSIX-style path to the flat binary image (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/zephyr/zephyr.bin`). null when not derivable.

sizeReport.description: POSIX-style path to the readelf-headers size/stat report (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/zephyr/zephyr.stat`, written only when `CONFIG_OUTPUT_STAT=y` -- same 'doesn't exist until built/enabled' caveat as every other artifact path here). null when not derivable.

symbols.description: POSIX-style path to the symbol-table dump (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/zephyr/zephyr.symbols`, written only when `CONFIG_OUTPUT_SYMBOLS=y`). null when not derivable.

compileCommands.description: POSIX-style path to `compile_commands.json` (Zephyr: `<buildDir>/build/compile_commands.json` -- `west build` drives Ninja and the top-level Zephyr CMakeLists.txt forces `CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS` unconditionally). null when the slice's runtime doesn't produce one at a predictable path -- which includes EVERY baremetal slice: its configure does pass `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`, but CMake implements that variable 'only by Makefile Generators and Ninja Generators. It is ignored on other generators' (CMake's own docs), and this plan does not choose the generator -- under the Visual Studio generator, the default on Windows, the file is never written at all.

outputDir.description: Additive under schemaVersion 1 (alplabai/tan-cli#550), like `envAppendPath`/`executionPolicy` before it -- absent from a plan emitted by a pre-#550 producer, which a consumer must treat exactly as null. POSIX-style path to the directory this slice's RUNTIME artifacts -- its `add_executable()` targets -- land in: `<buildDir>/output` for baremetal, pinned by the `-DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=$<1:...>` arg the slice's own configure carries (the generator expression is what stops a multi-config generator appending a per-config subdirectory, so the path holds on Visual Studio / Xcode / Ninja Multi-Config too). This is a deterministic PLACE TO LOOK, NOT a build-succeeded oracle: `CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` governs `add_executable` targets only, so an app built as `add_library(... STATIC ...)` plus a custom link/objcopy target builds cleanly and never creates this directory at all -- an empty or absent directory does not mean the slice produced nothing, and a consumer must not treat it as a failure signal. null for zephyr (the six named artifact paths above already index its tree) and yocto (its images land in the Yocto build tree's own deploy dir). This is a DIRECTORY, never a file: the target names inside are the app's own CMakeLists.txt to pick and are never invented here.

debug.description: Headless monitor/debug selectors for this slice (#610 §4): the console device selector + debug-probe selector a headless consumer needs, derived from board.yaml `diagnostics.console:` and the same flash-recipe fact `system-manifest.yaml`'s `slices[].flash_method`/`flash_args` already carry. null when unknown.

console.description: Resolved console backend selector: `uart` (Zephyr UART console), `ram` (Zephyr RAM console, read over SWD), or `linux` (Yocto/Ubuntu stdio/tty console). null when the slice inherits an unspecified board default (`diagnostics.console: none`/unset with no OS-derived default, e.g. a baremetal slice).

probe.description: Debug-probe runner selector for this slice: the explicitly-configured runner for a Zephyr slice's `zephyr_west_flash` recipe, else null -- meaning either the board.cmake default runner applies, or (Yocto image-flash, baremetal cmake-flash) this slice's runtime/flash recipe doesn't identify a live debug probe at all.

command.description: The build command to run for this slice, or null when this emitter has no valid command yet (see `slices` description; a matching `warnings` entry explains why).

tool.description: The executable's identity (e.g. 'west', 'bitbake', 'cmake') -- never a location; resolving it to a concrete path is the executor's job, not the plan's. No `pattern` is asserted here by design -- see the CHANGELOG and issue #1286.

cwd.description: POSIX-style working directory to run `tool` from; always equal to this slice's buildDir.

postCommands.description: Additive under schemaVersion 1 (alplabai/tan-cli#550), like `envAppendPath`/`executionPolicy` before it -- absent from a plan emitted by a pre-#550 producer, which a consumer must treat exactly as an empty array. Further commands the executor MUST run, IN ORDER, after `command` exits 0; the slice is built only once every one of them has. Empty for the runtimes whose single tool invocation configures AND builds (`west build`, `bitbake`), and always empty when `command` is null. A `baremetal` slice's `command` is a `cmake -S ... -B .` that only CONFIGURES, so its `cmake --build .` step lives here -- an executor that runs `command` alone reports a green build over a build tree with no object file, archive or executable in it, which is the defect this key exists to close. `executionPolicy` applies to each step exactly as it does to `command`. No `--parallel`/`-j`: job count is the consumer's scheduling policy, the same reason the plan carries no `sequential` key.

tool.description: The executable's identity, same contract as `command.tool` -- never a location.

cwd.description: POSIX-style working directory to run `tool` from; always equal to this slice's buildDir, same as `command.cwd`.

env.description: Environment variables the consumer must inject into the slice subprocess (handed to the subprocess environment verbatim once the consumer substitutes any token -- issue #865, `planPathMode: tokened`).

ALP_SDK_ROOT.description: The literal token `${SDK_ROOT}` under `planPathMode: tokened` (issue #865) -- tan-cli (PR #24) substitutes its own resolved alp-sdk checkout root before injecting this into the subprocess environment.

envAppendPath.description: SDK-owned env values the consumer must APPEND, skipping any value already present (de-dup first, matching `_alp_common.env_with_sdk` / `_workspace.subprocess_env`), to the slice subprocess env, distinct from `env` (set-verbatim). The join separator is PER-KEY, not uniformly os.pathsep: `EXTRA_ZEPHYR_MODULES` is a CMake list -- Zephyr's `zephyr_module.py` splits it on `;` on every platform, never an OS path list -- while `PYTHONPATH` is a real OS-native path list joined with `os.pathsep`. Plan wins / CLI fills gaps: a consumer that computes these itself should prefer the plan's values. Additive under schemaVersion 1; a new key so consumers pinned to an older shape safely ignore it. Values are `${SDK_ROOT}`-tokened under `planPathMode: tokened` (issue #865), substituted the same as `env.ALP_SDK_ROOT`.

sharedArtefacts.description: Cross-slice generated artefacts (e.g. generated/alp/system_ipc.h, dts-reservations.dtsi, dts-partitions.dtsi, and -- only when the project declares them -- alp_sysbuild.conf / sysbuild/tfm/tfm.conf). Conditional artefacts follow absence-emits-nothing: they appear only when their emit is non-empty. Byte-identical to what the Orchestrator's own materialise step writes under buildRoot.

path.description: POSIX-style path (under buildRoot) the consumer should write `contents` to.

contents.description: Full file contents, ready to byte-write verbatim.

warnings.description: Non-fatal planning warnings, one per affected core, machine-readable (`code`) plus a human-readable `message` so the consumer can surface -- or filter -- them without string-matching prose.

code.description: Stable machine-readable warning code. Known values as of schemaVersion 1: 'no-command' (missing app/board/image for the core's os), 'yocto-recipe-missing' (an app-only Yocto slice has app: but no recipe:, so there is no valid bitbake target), 'appdir-unrooted' (issue #865: a slice's `app:` resolves outside both `${PROJECT_ROOT}` and `${SDK_ROOT}`, so `appDir` is left as a genuine absolute path a consumer on a different checkout cannot re-root), 'board-tree-missing' (issue #999: a zephyr slice's `board:` names no tree under `zephyr/boards/alp/`, so no `west build -b <board>` command can be valid). New codes may be added without a schemaVersion bump -- consumers must not treat this as a closed enum.

coreId.description: The core this warning applies to (matches a `slices[].coreId`).

message.description: Human-readable explanation, safe to display verbatim.
